name: Guardian genius crossword No 161
preamble: The solution indicated by the wordplay in each of the 26 clues is lacking a required letter. Each letter of the alphabet is missing from a particular clue, though in four cases it is missing twiceand in one case four times.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Working at being asleep

blocks.note: the start of a word for working, carrying out a task
the letter the wordplay leaves out, as the preamble warns
the rest of the same word for working

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Working gives DOING; the missing Z (the classic snoring letter) goes in to make DOZING.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozing is sleeping lightly, so someone dozing is in a state of sleep.

clue.text: We left supporter hiding queen — that's a relief

indicators.note: something hiding another thing holds it inside itself

blocks.note: first of the two copies of the letter the wordplay leaves out
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
a fan supports a team
second copy of the omitted letter
HM, Her Majesty

explanation.surface: Someone relieved that a fan kept a queen out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ts of the answer are missing from the wordplay. In cricket the twelfth man is the substitute fielder, brought on in relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a substitute player, which is exactly the twelfth man's role in a cricket team.

clue.text: Trembled — is it come true? Oddly not

indicators.note: rejecting the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

blocks.note: the omitted letter, the first of four
the second letter of come
two more copies of the omitted letter
the fourth letter of come
the second and fourth letters of true
the last copy of the omitted letter

explanation.surface: A shaky question about whether something odd has come true.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters give only OERE; this is the clue missing its letter four times, and four Ds turn it into DODDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to move shakily, as the frail elderly do, so doddered means trembled.

clue.text: Light meat

blocks.note: the opening of the cured pork meat
the letter the wordplay leaves out
the rest of the same cured meat

explanation.surface: A description of lean meat, light rather than fatty.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat gives BACON; the missing E makes BEACON.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire or lamp, a light used as a warning or guide.

clue.text: Support from nastier bullying

indicators.note: bullying pushes things about roughly, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeking backing from someone who is being even more of a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give ANISTER; the missing B goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail of a staircase, something you hold for support.

clue.text: Got little bear to carry the can

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

blocks.note: the omitted letter, the first of two
Ted, short for teddy, a small bear
a tin is a can
the second copy of the omitted letter

explanation.surface: A small bear was made to take the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Both As of the answer are missing from the wordplay. To carry the can is a British idiom for taking the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Attained means achieved or reached, and got is a plain synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Rushing quickly into second courtship

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the start of the word for courting
the letter the wordplay leaves out
the rest of the same word for courting

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying headlong into a second romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Second and courtship give S + WOOING; the missing P makes SWOOPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Swooping is diving or descending swiftly, as a bird of prey does on its target.

clue.text: I live alongside an animal

blocks.note: taken as written
to be is to exist or live
the letter the wordplay leaves out

explanation.surface: A person sharing a home with a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: I + BE gives IBE; the missing X ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat of the Alps and Asia, one example of an animal.

clue.text: Dropping belt, thong … that's the idea

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a G-string is a thong
a belt in the sense of an encircling band or zone, a ring
the letter the wordplay leaves out

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off belt and skimpy underwear, with a remark about the point of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A thong is a G-string, and a belt in the sense of a band or zone is a ring; the missing I goes after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist is the essential point or main sense of something, its central idea.

clue.text: One fool, then another

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
the Roman numeral for one
a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: Pointing out one idiot after another.
explanation.walkthrough: One fool gives I + TWIT; the missing N goes in front. The definition 'another' means another fool, leaning on the fool just named.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly person, so it is another word for fool.

clue.text: Felicity's younger and playing indoors

indicators.note: playing about with something leaves it in a different order
something indoors is inside, so it goes within the other part

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
St James the Less is also called James the Younger, so less can mean younger
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called Felicity is the younger sister and plays inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felicity' looks like a girl's name but is the definition. The missing G goes in front of the wordplay's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity means happiness, and gladness is a synonym for that state of joy.

clue.text: It shows change in opinion of regiments marching around ring

indicators.note: troops marching move about, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a ring is round like the letter O
the letter the wordplay leaves out

explanation.surface: Something that registers how views shift among soldiers on the march.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give SINGOMETER; the missing W comes second. The swingometer is the British TV election-night graphic showing voting swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A swingometer displays the swing in votes between parties, a measure of shifting public opinion.

clue.text: Amazing half day with lads — nearly got up late

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut
in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first half of Monday, a day
the letter the wordplay leaves out
lads are young men
late without its last letter

explanation.surface: An amazing half-day out with friends who got up late.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is missing only the U, which sits after the half day.
explanation.definitionFit: Monumental means enormous or remarkable in scale, so it is a strong synonym for amazing.

clue.text: One taking over might thus greet clarinettist

blocks.note: a casual hello
the letter the wordplay leaves out
Acker Bilk, the British jazz clarinettist

explanation.surface: A hijacker might say hello to a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hi, Acker' is how you might greet Acker Bilk, the clarinettist behind 'Stranger on the Shore'; the missing J goes after HI.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijacker seizes control of a vehicle or plane, literally taking it over.

clue.text: The woman leads me into a train carriage — that's sweet

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside

blocks.note: a van is a railway carriage for goods or luggage
the letter the wordplay leaves out
her refers to a woman
me, the speaker, is I

explanation.surface: A woman shepherding someone onto a train, with a sentimental verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman leads, so her word comes before the word for me, and the pair goes into the carriage; the missing C follows the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacherin is a dessert of meringue layers with cream and fruit, so it is a sweet.

clue.text: "Paradise" sooner reached?

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before or sooner
the start of a word for reached or gained
the letter the wordplay leaves out
the rest of the same word for reached

explanation.surface: Asking whether heaven will be reached earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: ERE + WON gives EREWON; the missing H goes after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Erewhon is Samuel Butler's satirical utopia, its name nowhere roughly backwards, so a paradise in quotes.

clue.text: Dug out Wodehouse compilation that's no use

indicators.note: with no use, the letters of that word are struck out
a compilation gathers material and puts it together afresh

blocks.note: the author's name without the letters of use
the omitted letter, needed twice

explanation.surface: A useless P. G. Wodehouse anthology that has been rummaged out.
explanation.walkthrough: The reworked letters give HOOWED; both Ls are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hollow something out is to dig or scoop out its inside, so hollowed means dug out.

clue.text: Soup produced first, then a wine

blocks.note: to produce is to make
Soup is the setter, who refers to themself as I
the letter the wordplay leaves out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef making soup to start, followed by a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soup produced' would be I MADE; putting produced first gives MADE I, then A, for MADEIA; the missing R goes before the A. Soup is this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Drink tea, out of it from methaqualone high

indicators.note: out of it means taken out of the longer word
someone high is scrambled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, the name of a sedative drug
taken as written, the letters to remove
the omitted letter, needed twice

explanation.surface: A drink and a cup of tea for someone spaced out on a sedative drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give LEMONQUAH; both Ss are missing. Methaqualone is the sedative sold as Quaaludes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon squash is a soft drink, a concentrated lemon cordial diluted with water.

clue.text: Old computer made in the Gulf

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
Atari made home computers and games consoles in the 1970s and 80s

explanation.surface: A vintage computer manufactured in the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: The old computer gives ATARI; the missing Q goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatari means from Qatar, a state on the Persian Gulf, so describes goods produced there.

clue.text: Premieres of Industrial Light and Magic movie

indicators.note: a premiere is a first showing, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
first letters of Industrial, Light and Magic

explanation.surface: First screenings of a film made with Industrial Light and Magic effects.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters give ILM, which is also the special-effects company's abbreviation; the missing F goes in front. The word 'and' gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Film and movie are synonyms for a motion picture.

clue.text: Close sale

definitions.note: vend is used here as a noun, an old word for a sale

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
a close is an end

explanation.surface: A sale about to end.
explanation.walkthrough: Close gives END; the missing V goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Vend usually means to sell, and as a noun it means a sale in Chambers.

clue.text: Put topping on cake — daughter gets stuck in

blocks.note: to ice is to cover with icing
the start of a small round cake
the letter the wordplay leaves out
the rest of the same cake
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter tucks into a cake after icing it.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE + BUN + D gives ICEBUND; the missing O goes after the B. 'Gets stuck in' looks like one idiom for eating, but gets is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebound means trapped or frozen in by ice, as a ship can be, so stuck in.

clue.text: Author speaks to erudite in-crowd

indicators.note: the letters are taken from in among the crowd of words that follow

blocks.note: the end of speaks
taken as written
the letter the wordplay leaves out
the first letter of erudite
the second letter of erudite

explanation.surface: A writer addresses the clever clique.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the words speaks, to and erudite, and need the missing K to complete the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker is the Irish writer who wrote Dracula, so an author.

clue.text: Two girls, rather old

blocks.note: the letter the wordplay leaves out
the first girl's name
the second girl's name

explanation.surface: A pair of girls who are somewhat elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: The two girls' names are run together; the missing M goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval is used loosely to mean old-fashioned or antiquated, so it means rather old.

clue.text: Manage GP's first practice

blocks.note: a GP, a family doctor, is a Dr
the letter the wordplay leaves out
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A family doctor's priority is running the surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'GP's first' puts the doctor before the word for manage; the missing Y goes between them. A GP is a British family doctor, whose surgery is called a practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal or trial before the real thing, a piece of practice.
